task_instance: Create a Slack emoji GIF (128x128, animated) of a spinning, pulsing gold star with glow and sparkles, per the user request pattern 'make me a GIF of X doing Y for Slack'
evidence: The skill's SKILL.md references core utilities (core.gif_builder, core.validators, core.frame_composer, core.easing) but the actual source files for these were not present in the ce_sources skill directory (only SKILL.md and LICENSE existed). I reimplemented minimal versions of GIFBuilder (frame collection + GIF save with palette quantization, duplicate-frame removal, duration-from-fps) and validate_gif/is_slack_ready (checks dimensions, animation, size, duration) matching the documented interfaces, at /tmp/.../gif_builder.py and /tmp/.../validators.py. Installed dependencies via `pip install pillow imageio numpy` (succeeded). Wrote make_star_gif.py which builds 24 frames (12fps, ~1.92s) of a gold 5-pointed star that spins (rotation via math.sin/cos angle offsets), pulses (scale via sine wave 0.85-1.15x), has a semi-transparent glow layer, a smaller counter-rotating inner star for depth, a vertical gradient background, and 4 orbiting sparkle dots -- built entirely with PIL ImageDraw primitives (polygon/ellipse) as the skill instructs (no emoji fonts, no pre-packaged graphics). Ran `python3 make_star_gif.py` successfully, producing star.gif (50023 bytes, 128x128, 24 frames). Verified programmatically with validate_gif(): size_ok=True, dimensions_ok=True (128x128), is_animated=True (24 frames), duration_ok=True (1.92s < 3.5s emoji threshold) -> overall PASS. Also extracted frame 0 as PNG and visually inspected it (Read tool rendered the image): shows a polished gold star with dark outline, inner highlight star, and white sparkle dots on a purple gradient background, matching the 'looks polished, not basic' quality bar in the skill doc.
